Age and sex influence seed dispersal of native and non-native plants by Lion-tailed Macaques Macaca silenus. bioRxiv 2024.12.09.627456, version 1. https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.12.09.627456. Claims are paraphrased; this is a preprint not certified by peer review.

claims.text: Among sampled Western Ghats lion-tailed macaques, the study recovered mitochondrial clades north and south of the Palghat Gap; a fossil-calibrated analysis of 893 bases estimated a mean 2.11 million years to their most recent common ancestor. At eight Anamalai forest fragments, sampled HVR-I diversity was lower than at a nearby continuous-forest site.
claims.scope: Regional mitochondrial markers and named sample sites; the time estimate is not a genome-wide species split date or current viability assessment.

claims.text: Over 480 follow-hours in February–May 2016, researchers followed one free-ranging troop across four habitat types; active foraging was higher in an open patch and forest edge than in forest interior and lower in the human settlement. The study also recorded plant parts from 19 species and non-plant foods.
claims.scope: One habituated troop at Puthuthottam during one dry season; not a species-wide habitat or diet estimate.

claims.text: A bioRxiv v1 study reports 375.9 focal-watch hours across four troops at one 92-hectare fragment; sampled subadults consumed a greater diversity of native and non-native fruits than adults and dispersed fewer Ficus seeds than adult females.
claims.scope: Single site, one dry season, field year not reported; preprint not certified by peer review.

gaps: No new multi-source dossier or external expert review is produced by this reader-guide update.
The studies are geographically and seasonally bounded; they do not provide a current range-wide census, population trend, complete diet, or species-wide behavioural response.
